problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set 
${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.
worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{1\cdot 2+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 2}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{4}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{1\cdot 1+4\cdot (-4)+3\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =\frac{4}{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(4[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
